confidence_basis: Main PDF, OpenDataLoader output, pypdf fallback snippets, rendered figure/methods pages, extracted figure images, and the downloaded supplement DOC/text extraction were checked. Experiments 4-6 are extractable as three separable designs: Exp. 4 hand-versus-trunk with the hand on the chest, Exp. 5 hand near-versus-far from the trunk, and Exp. 6 face-versus-trunk congruent/incongruent sound-location cells. Trajectory distances, speeds, tactile anchors, baseline/catch logic, repetitions, ITI jitter, and total trial counts are reported or directly derived. Remaining uncertainty concerns exact original WAVs for all setups, exact 16-speaker source/gain details, exact SOA milliseconds, block/order rules, response timeout, and whether a single composite profile should be split before implementation.

profile_recreation_assessment.reason: The publication reports enough Segment 1-4 information to recreate Exp. 4, Exp. 5, and Exp. 6 as separate PPS profiles. Exp. 4/5 can use the reported two-speaker pink-noise near/far setup at 22 cm/s; Exp. 6 can use a renderer-emulated or multi-source 16-speaker front-space profile at 25 cm/s with face/trunk sound-location congruency. Exact author stimulus files, some gain details, block/order rules, and response timeout remain approximations.

orientation_ledger.participant_frame: Exp. 4: right hand adjacent to chest at sternum level; Exp. 5: right hand near or far from trunk; Exp. 6: participant stood at the end of the 16-speaker array. Explicit gaze/facing instruction is not reported.
orientation_ledger.room_apparatus_frame: Exp. 4/5 used a two-speaker near-far line with near around 5 cm and far around 100 cm. Exp. 6 used the 16-speaker array with seven front-space distances and the farthest speaker at 2 m.
orientation_ledger.body_relative_mapping: Exp. 4/5 map sound distance relative to the hand/trunk posture. Exp. 6 maps sound location as face-directed or trunk-directed and touch location as face or trunk, creating congruent and incongruent audio-tactile cells.
orientation_ledger.tactile_anchor: Exp. 4 uses hand dorsum and upper chest/sternum tactile targets; Exp. 5 uses hand dorsum; Exp. 6 uses forehead for peri-face and upper chest/sternum for peri-trunk.
orientation_ledger.movement_implementation: Exp. 4/5 use coactivated two-speaker differential intensity for apparent continuous looming/receding motion. Exp. 6 uses a physical 16-speaker array with time-varying speaker intensities.
orientation_ledger.evidence_class: Main-text methods/results, Figure 4/Figure 5 visual inspection, Figure 1 apparatus caption, supplement two-speaker provenance, and pypdf fallback checks.

source_checks.scope: PDF pages 5-8 for Experiments 4-6 and Figures 4-5; pages 11-13 for participants, tactile apparatus, acoustic stimuli, procedure, design, counts, table, and ITI.
Used as the primary extracted-text map for targeted searches over Experiment 4, Experiment 5, Experiment 6, acoustic stimuli, procedure, design, baselines, catches, and counts.
Visual inspection of the shared two-speaker/16-speaker setup figure plus the Exp. 4/5 and Exp. 6 body-part geometry figures.
Checked local supplement for two-speaker provenance, loudspeaker model, pink-noise source class, SoundForge shaping, dB endpoints, and validation details.
Searched for two-speaker, 16-speaker, hand, trunk, face, pink-noise, SoundForge, SPL, M-Audio, validation, and apparatus terms.
Printed targeted snippets from PDF pages 5-8 and 11-13 to verify experiment separation, body-part conditions, acoustic setup, tactile apparatus, count formulas, and ITI.
Temporary rendered pages checked for figure/caption geometry, methods wording, and design/count paragraphs; page images were not committed.

review_attempts.result: Mapped 20/25 auto-mined candidate fields and identified cross-experiment contamination that required hand separation of Exp. 4, Exp. 5, and Exp. 6.
Separated two-speaker Exp. 4/5 pink-noise apparent motion from the 16-speaker Exp. 6 face/trunk sound-location setup and recorded their different speeds and distance grids.
Inspected Figure 1, Figure 4, Figure 5, and rendered pages; recorded participant/apparatus/body-relative mappings in the orientation ledger.
pypdf snippets confirmed Exp. 4/5/6 text on hand/trunk/face conditions, 22 cm/s and 25 cm/s speeds, tactile-device placement, count formulas, and 500-700 ms ITI.
Supplement supplied the two-speaker M-Audio/pink-noise/SoundForge/55-70 dB provenance used for Exp. 4/5; it did not resolve exact 16-speaker source files or gain law for Exp. 6.

review_attempts.strategy: Trial sequence, baseline, catch, and count pass
review_attempts.result: Identified the three task families, D1/D6 or D1/D7 tactile-only baselines, sound-only catches, Exp. 4/5/6 repetition factors, derived baseline/catch counts, and explicit total trial counts.
Checked Canzoneri et al. 2012 lineage and the supplement route; preserved unresolved values for exact original WAVs, exact SOA milliseconds, block/order rules, and response timeout.

stimulus_type.value: Exp. 4/5 use 44.1 kHz pink-noise samples in the shared two-speaker setup; Exp. 6 uses dynamic auditory stimuli in the 16-speaker setup, with exact waveform not separately specified.
stimulus_type.page_or_section: Supplement, 2-speakers setup; PDF p.11 Acoustic Stimuli
stimulus_type.evidence_note: Pink-noise provenance is direct for the two-speaker setup; Exp. 6 16-speaker waveform remains less explicit.

source_provenance.value: Two-speaker stimuli were SoundForge-shaped pink-noise samples; 16-speaker source asset/noise seed/generation files were not found in PDF or supplement.
source_provenance.evidence_note: The source class is known for Exp. 4/5; exact author files are missing, especially for Exp. 6.

trajectory_count.value: Exp. 4: two body-part blocks x looming/receding; Exp. 5: near/far hand postures with looming only; Exp. 6: face/trunk sound location x face/trunk touch location x looming/receding.
trajectory_count.page_or_section: PDF pp.5-7, Experiments 4-6; p.13 count formulas
trajectory_count.evidence_note: Composite record contains three designs; split profiles are preferable for implementation.

trajectory_path.value: Exp. 4/5 sample D1-D6 at 5, 24, 43, 62, 81, 100 cm over a near-far 100 cm two-speaker line; Exp. 6 samples D1-D7 at 5, 37, 69, 101, 133, 165, 197 cm in front space.
trajectory_path.page_or_section: PDF pp.5-7 and p.11; Figure 1 caption/setup image
trajectory_path.evidence_note: Exp. 6 subjects stood at the end of the array, with the farthest speaker at 2 m.

stimulus_duration.value: Exp. 4/5 full path duration is about 4.55 s from 100 cm at 22 cm/s; Exp. 6 full front-space path is about 8.0 s from 2 m at 25 cm/s.
stimulus_duration.evidence_note: Derived from reported path spans and speeds; no separate audio-file duration table was found.

stimulus_speed.value: Exp. 4 and Exp. 5 sounds traveled at 22 cm/s; Exp. 6 sounds moved at 25 cm/s.
stimulus_speed.evidence_note: The methods explicitly separate the two-speaker and 16-speaker speeds.

auditory_conditions.value: Exp. 4 used looming/receding sounds; Exp. 5 used looming only; Exp. 6 used looming/receding sounds directed toward face or trunk for congruent/incongruent cells.
auditory_conditions.page_or_section: PDF pp.5-7, Experiments 4-6; p.11 Acoustic Stimuli
auditory_conditions.evidence_note: Exp. 6 sound direction was within-subject, while sound/touch locations were between-subject factors.

gain_envelope.value: Two-speaker looming rose exponentially from 55 to 70 dB SPL and receding reversed this pattern; Exp. 6 reports time-varying speaker intensities but not exact 16-speaker gain endpoints.
gain_envelope.page_or_section: Supplement, 2-speakers setup; PDF p.11 Acoustic Stimuli
gain_envelope.evidence_note: Good for Exp. 4/5 recreation; 16-speaker envelope remains a caveat.

renderer_or_apparatus.value: Exp. 4/5 used two coactivated loudspeakers; Exp. 6 used a physical 16-speaker array with seven front-space distances and time-varying speaker intensities.
renderer_or_apparatus.page_or_section: PDF p.11 Acoustic Stimuli; Figure 1 setup image
renderer_or_apparatus.evidence_note: Figure 1 visually confirms both apparatus families.

trial_rows_families.value: Three trial families across Exp. 4-6: bimodal audio-tactile trials, tactile-only unimodal baseline trials, and auditory-only catch/no-go trials.
trial_rows_families.page_or_section: PDF p.12, General Procedure and Design and Analysis
trial_rows_families.evidence_note: The design section lists the shared task families used across experiments.

condition_intermixing.value: Trial families are combined within experiment formulas; Exp. 4 body part is in separate blocks, Exp. 5 near/far posture is a condition, and Exp. 6 sound/touch locations are between-subject cells.
condition_intermixing.evidence_note: The paper reports condition structure but not a complete trial randomization algorithm.

blocked_or_random_order.value: Exp. 4 explicitly assessed hand and trunk in separate blocks; Exp. 6 used a between-subject sound-location x touch-location design. Exact block order is not reported.
blocked_or_random_order.evidence_note: Exp. 5 posture ordering and exact trial order remain unresolved.

iti_jitter_policy.value: Inter-trial intervals were randomly shuffled between 500 and 700 ms.
iti_jitter_policy.evidence_note: Reported as a general rule after the experiment-specific formulas.

response_window.evidence_note: XBOX button response and 125 Hz sampling are reported, but no numeric response timeout/window was found.

task_sequence_rules.value: Participants responded rapidly to tactile vibration, ignored sounds, and withheld responses on sound-only catches; baseline trials were tactile-only.
task_sequence_rules.page_or_section: PDF p.12, General Procedure and Design and Analysis
task_sequence_rules.evidence_note: Catch trials were included to prevent automatic responding and monitor attention.

tactile_stimulus.value: Precision MicroDrives 312-101 motor, 150 Hz, 100 ms stimulation; Exp. 4 chest or hand dorsum, Exp. 5 hand dorsum, Exp. 6 forehead or upper chest/sternum.
tactile_stimulus.evidence_note: Methods report motor model, 3 V, 60 mA, 9000 rpm, 5 g, 113 mm2 surface, and 50 ms spin-up.

soa_table.value: Use distance-at-touch grids as SOA anchors: Exp. 4/5 D1-D6 at 5-100 cm and 22 cm/s; Exp. 6 D1-D7 at 5-197 cm and 25 cm/s, reversed for looming versus receding.
soa_table.page_or_section: PDF pp.5-7, p.11, p.12 Design and Analysis
soa_table.evidence_note: Exact millisecond SOAs are not tabulated, but distance/speed mappings are sufficient to derive them.

baseline_strategy.value: Tactile-only unimodal baseline trials without sound; fastest baseline condition was subtracted from each participant's audio-tactile RTs.
baseline_strategy.evidence_note: The baseline correction strategy is described for all experiments.

baseline_timing.value: Exp. 4/5 baselines correspond to D1 and D6 equivalent timings; Exp. 6 baselines correspond to D1 and D7 equivalent timings.
baseline_timing.page_or_section: PDF pp.12-13, Design and Analysis and formulas
baseline_timing.evidence_note: Baseline rows are reported by D endpoints; exact milliseconds should be derived from path/speed.

catch_trial_type.value: Auditory-only catch trials presented sound without tactile stimulation and required response withholding.
catch_trial_type.page_or_section: PDF pp.12-13, Design and Analysis and Table 1
catch_trial_type.evidence_note: Table 1 reports catch withholding accuracy for Exp. 4-6 conditions.

repetitions_per_tactile_soa_condition.value: Exp. 4: formula x16 repetitions; Exp. 5: formula x24 repetitions; Exp. 6: formula x16 repetitions for each participant's assigned sound/touch-location cell.
repetitions_per_tactile_soa_condition.evidence_note: The reported formulas specify repetition factors for each experiment.

baseline_count.value: Exp. 4: 2 baselines x 2 body parts x16 = 64; Exp. 5: 2 baselines x2 postures x24 = 96; Exp. 6: 2 baselines x2 directions x16 = 64.
baseline_count.page_or_section: PDF p.13, Design and Analysis formulas
baseline_count.evidence_note: Derived from endpoint baseline rows and repetition factors.

catch_count.value: Formula residuals imply Exp. 4: 32 catches; Exp. 5: 48 catches; Exp. 6: 32 catches. Direction/posture split for catches is not fully detailed.
catch_count.page_or_section: PDF p.13, Design and Analysis formulas; Table 1
catch_count.evidence_note: Counts follow from totals after multisensory and baseline rows.

block_count.value: Exp. 4 had separate hand and trunk blocks; Exp. 6 used between-subject sound/touch-location cells. Exact run block count/order for Exp. 4-6 is not fully reported.
block_count.page_or_section: PDF pp.5-7, p.11, pp.12-13; supplement searched
block_count.evidence_note: Enough condition phases are known for recreation, but not exact block sequencing.

total_trial_count.value: Exp. 4 consisted of 480 trials; Exp. 5 consisted of 432 trials; Exp. 6 consisted of 320 trials.
total_trial_count.evidence_note: Totals are explicitly reported in the experiment-specific formulas.

critical_caveats: This record bundles three distinct designs; profile recreation should split Exp. 4, Exp. 5, and Exp. 6 rather than make one composite task.
Exact original pink-noise WAV/noise seed and SoundForge envelope files are not provided.
Exp. 6 16-speaker waveform, SPL calibration, and exact gain/intensity field are not reported beyond time-varying speaker intensities.
Exact SOA milliseconds are derived from reported distance/speed mappings rather than printed in a table.
Exact trial-order randomization, block order, and response timeout/window are not reported.
Exp. 5 posture order and catch-trial split by posture/direction are not explicit.
Participant gaze/facing direction is not explicitly stated; body-relative mapping follows author labels and figure geometry.
The two-speaker supplement provenance applies cleanly to Exp. 4/5, but only partially informs Exp. 6.
next_manual_action: Create three separate implementation candidates: Exp. 4 hand-on-trunk body-part comparison, Exp. 5 peri-hand near/far posture comparison, and Exp. 6 face/trunk congruency profile. Use reported distance grids, speeds, baselines, ITI, and counts; treat original stimulus files, exact 16-speaker gain field, exact SOA milliseconds, block order, and response timeout as approximations.
